title: Personal Outcomes Canvas — Weekly Sprint Scratch
content:
Purpose: quick, low-friction canvas for tracking 1) outcome-level goals for the quarter, 2) the weekly sprint commitments that ladder to them, and 3) a tiny retrospective/learning log. Use as a scratchpad — not polished.

Guiding principle: focus on signals, not vanity counts. I want 3 outcome signals this quarter and 2 micro-experiments per week. If a thing doesn't move a signal after 2 weeks, archive it.

Quarterly Outcomes (draft) — Q1 2026
- Outcome A: Reduce per-feature inference latency for the customer-facing playground by 20% under 512-token requests.
  - Signal: median P95 latency (ms) for playground route /api/generate (512 tokens). Current: 320ms. Target: 256ms.
  - Secondary: tail (99th) under 600ms.
- Outcome B: Improve quality-stability for the internal ridgeline eval set (3 critical prompts).
  - Signal: % of prompts passing golden threshold (token-level KL, human check). Current: 72%. Target: 85%.
- Outcome C: Personal throughput — finish two deep-dive writeups and one public reference notebook.
  - Signal: drafts completed and PRs opened.

Monthly levers (ideas to move signals)
- Optimize batching configuration for small-concurrent bursts (in Redwood Dedicated config). Hypothesis: reduce small-req latency by enabling aggressive continuous batching with 40ms hold.
- Add prefix KV caching for the playground common prompts (top-50 requests). Hypothesis: cache hits reduce median by ~25%.
- Tighten model rollout to include a guarded kernel selection that falls back earlier for cold-starts.

Weekly Sprint Template (use and copy each week)
- Week of: YYYY-MM-DD
- Focus (one sentence): e.g., "Tune playground batching + validate latency on staging."
- 3 Commitments (small, measurable)
  1) Update Dedicated policy + run small-scale load test (3k reqs).
  2) Implement prefix cache for top-10 playground prompts and run A/B.
  3) Write observation note and add to team-runbook.
- Confidence (1–5): 3
- Blockers / needs: e.g., "Need SRE window Friday 10–12; need model weights from research team."
- Quick retrospective: what moved? numbers?

Example log — Week of 2025-11-10
- Focus: prototype prefix cache, measure impact on median/99.
- Commitments status:
  1) Dedicated policy: done. Updated autoscale min 2 -> 3, hold 40ms. Preliminary median down to 285ms (staging).
  2) Prefix cache: partial. Implemented cache shim for top-5 prompts, hit rate ~14% in first run. Median down to 270ms for cached cohort.
  3) Observation note: drafted. Need rough cost estimate.
- Learnings:
  - Hit rate is highly sensitive to prompt normalization; need canonicalization step.
  - Continuous batching hold affects tail latency more than median — experiment with 20/40/80ms.
- Actions next week:
  - Add prompt normalization, expand to top-25, run 10k request test.
  - Add cost calc to runbook.

Mini-experiment checklist (template)
- Hypothesis (one line)
- Change (code/config)
- Metric(s) monitored (primary signal + guardrail)
- Test size and duration
- Rollback criteria
- Outcome and learning

Personal retrospective (monthly quick scan)
- Wins: broken down by outcome A/B/C. E.g., "Batch hold tweak produced -15% median in staging."
- Misses: what I underestimated (coordination, test data).
- What I will stop doing: low-impact manual tuning without clear signal.
- What I will start doing: stricter pre-commit checklists for latency runs (description, seed traffic, expected delta).

Signals tracker (living list)
- Playground median (512) — baseline 320ms — weekly pulled from observability.
- Playground 99th — baseline 780ms.
- Ridgeline eval pass rate — baseline 72%.
- Docs drafts — baseline 0/3.

Notes to self / scratch items
- Quick wins to try when blocked: turn on 8-bit quantization on a small variant + sanity-run; sometimes saves 10–18% on latency.
- Remind: schedule 1:1 with Amelia to sync on rollout policy (she suggested a canary threshold idea).
- Jira: JIRA-ENG-2412 is the tracking ticket for the prefix-cache spike test. Link it in runbook.

Unresolved questions
- Is the production telemetry sampling reliable for short bursts? If not, how to get accurate P95 for small windows?@observability-team
- Do we have any cost model for caching that includes GPU memory pressure? If not, talk to infra.

Quick checklist before publishing a public note
- Include simple graph (median+99) and test parameters
- Attach PRs and runbook link
- Add short TL;DR for non-technical reader

End note: keep this doc short and replace weekly sections as I go. Archive experiments that don't get at least a 5% improvement on primary signal after two iterations.

-- Joel
